protocol.name: glassine_handwriting_v1

description.summary: handwriting for an app's writing surface: raw and neat ink, text

protocol.description:
The pen interface of GlassineOS handwriting (GlassineOS/handwriting spec 004, and the neat ink layer of spec 003). An app turns it on for a surface; the compositor then passes each pen stroke written there to the app as a vector stroke when the pen lifts, and, with the handwriting service behind it, the stroke's neatened version, readings while the person writes and ranked candidates at a pause. The app reports what the person did with a reading; that is the confirmation the person's samples learn from.
The compositor identifies the app (its sandbox's application id, or the program it runs), never the app itself, and sends the service only what the surface turned on: nothing with both neatening and text off, nothing at all for a private field. The pen's preview on the panel stays the raw stroke (glassine_ink_v1); the app draws whichever version it keeps with its next frame.
The same pen events still reach the app through the tablet protocol as before; this interface adds the strokes as the compositor saw them, numbered, so that readings and neatened strokes can name them.
Points are arrays of 6 int32 per point, in this order: x and y (wl_fixed, surface coordinates, y down), the time (milliseconds, the tablet events' clock), the pressure (0..65535, 0 when the tool reports none) and the tilt in x and y (wl_fixed, degrees from the vertical, 0 when the tool reports none): the values the tablet protocol sends. A stroke's points come in parts, so that no message outgrows the wire: zero or more points events, each with at most 128 points, then the stroke or neat_stroke event that ends them. Strings in events are at most 1024 bytes.
Version 2 adds writing regions (GlassineOS/handwriting spec 005): any number of handwritten fields on one surface (glassine_handwriting_region_v1), each with its own area, ruled lines, field type, languages, reading and neatening, whose reading is the field's value. An app bound at version 1 never sees any of it and keeps the behaviour above. Payloads that can outgrow a message (a value's text, the saved state, stroke numbers, the outline of a word set in the person's font) travel as data parts of at most 2048 bytes, gathered until the message that takes them.
Sizes: the compositor gives the service the px per millimetre of the output the pen writes on (GlassineOS/handwriting spec 004 FR-017): from the output's physical size, else from the person's setting for that output; without either the units stay the pen's own and the service applies its documented default density.

interface.name: glassine_handwriting_manager_v1

description.summary: handwriting surfaces

interface.description: On bind the compositor sends capabilities and the languages, then done; again whenever they change (the service starts or stops, a letter model appears).

entry.name: already_exists
entry.summary: the surface has a handwriting object

request.name: get_handwriting

description.summary: the pen interface for a surface

request.description: At most one per wl_surface. It does not take the surface's ink areas (glassine_ink_v1, one per surface): an app, or the GTK ink module, may set those as before. A new object has neatening and text off and the whole surface as its area: it passes on raw strokes only.

entry.name: strokes
entry.summary: raw strokes (always)

entry.name: neaten
entry.summary: neatened strokes (the service is there)

entry.name: text
entry.summary: readings and candidates (the service is there)

entry.name: letters
entry.summary: the person has a letter model: neatening pulls letters to it, not only the line

entry.name: regions
entry.summary: writing regions are read: values, candidates, gestures, word layout (the service is there and reads regions). Only sent to a manager bound at version 2 or later; without it regions still route raw strokes

description.summary: a language that can be read, in the service's order
the capabilities and languages above are complete

interface.name: glassine_handwriting_v1

description.summary: the pen interface on one surface

interface.description:
Choices take effect for strokes that start after them, except set_neaten, which also neatens again the writing the surface holds (a change of strength without new pen input). Strokes are numbered from 0 per object and never reused; clear empties what the object holds without restarting the numbers.
From version 2 the object can hold writing regions (get_region). Once it has made one, the object is in region mode for good: its own area, guides, choices, clear and report no longer act, it sends no stroke, neat_stroke, reading or candidate events itself, and every stroke goes to the region it starts in (glassine_handwriting_region_v1). A stroke that starts outside every region is not delivered through this interface; the tablet events still reach the app as before.

description.summary: nothing more is sent; the service forgets the surface's ink

request.name: set_area

description.summary: where strokes count, in surface coordinates

request.description: A stroke counts when it starts inside the region. The region is copied. Null: the whole surface.

request.name: set_guides

description.summary: the area's ruled lines

request.description: The lines the writing sits on: the first at y first (wl_fixed, surface coordinates), the next ones every spacing below it. Neatening goes line by line; each stroke belongs to the line it is written on, a descender reaching a little below its guide. spacing 0 (the start): no guides, the lines are found from the writing.

request.name: set_neaten

description.summary: neatening on or off, and its strength

request.description: strength 0 to 1 (wl_fixed, clamped): 0 passes the raw strokes as neat strokes, 1 the neatest. Turning it on, or a new strength, neatens the writing held again.

description.summary: readings and candidates on or off (off: none are made for this surface)

entry.name: password
entry.summary: private: nothing is sent to the service

entry.name: pin
entry.summary: private: nothing is sent to the service

request.name: set_context

description.summary: the field the writing goes into

request.description: purpose and hints as in zwp_text_input_v3 (the values are the same), the text before and after the cursor (UTF-8, at most 4000 bytes each, the end nearest the cursor kept), languages a comma-separated list in order (empty: the person's setting). Takes effect for the next piece of writing (after clear or a report).

description.summary: the app is done with the writing held: it is forgotten

entry.name: picked
entry.summary: the person picked candidate rank of the reading

entry.name: accepted
entry.summary: the person accepted the reading's best candidate

entry.name: corrected
entry.summary: the person corrected it to text

entry.name: discarded
entry.summary: the person threw the writing away

request.name: report

description.summary: what the person did with a reading

request.description: serial names the candidates (candidates_done). picked: rank is the candidate's (0 best), text its text; accepted: rank 0; corrected: text is what the person made of it; discarded: text empty. A pick, an acceptance or a correction stores the raw strokes of that reading with the text as one of the person's samples, when the person allows this app to learn and the field learns; the writing is then forgotten as with clear. The answer is report_done.

entry.name: raw
entry.summary: for a stroke event

entry.name: neat
entry.summary: for a neat_stroke event

event.name: points

description.summary: a part of a stroke's points

event.name: stroke

description.summary: a raw stroke, sent when the pen lifts

event.description: Every stroke that starts in the area, as the tablet reported it: the points events just before it. Sent by the compositor itself, without the service.

entry.name: kept
entry.summary: passed unchanged (drawing, a gesture, not read)

entry.name: line
entry.summary: line-level corrections only

entry.name: pulled
entry.summary: also pulled towards the person's letters

event.name: neat_stroke

description.summary: the neatened version of a raw stroke

event.description: Replaces raw stroke stroke (or its earlier neat_stroke): the points events just before it, the same points with only x and y moved. Sent once the writing it belongs to is read, and again when later strokes or a new strength change it.

event.name: reading

description.summary: a partial reading while the person writes (text on)

event.description: The best reading of the strokes so far; a newer one replaces it. strokes: the stroke numbers it covers (array of uint32), at most the last 512 of them.

entry.name: ink
entry.summary: the ink's own best reading

entry.name: beam
entry.summary: another reading of the ink

entry.name: words
entry.summary: a word of the list one edit from a reading

entry.name: guided
entry.summary: the search the words guided

event.name: candidate

description.summary: one ranked candidate at a pause (text on)

event.description: rank 0 is the best. fit 1 when a pick of it is stored as it is, 0 when it would be checked and not pass. chars: per character of text, the strokes that make it, as in the recognizer's reading (docs/recognizer.md ALIGN, with this object's stroke numbers): entries separated by ";", each stroke N or N:A-B (points A to B); empty when it would be longer than 1024 bytes.

event.name: candidates_done

description.summary: the candidates above (count of them) are complete

event.description: serial names them in report. count 0: nothing could be read.

entry.name: stored
entry.summary: kept as a sample

entry.name: not_kept
entry.summary: nothing to keep: discarded, a field that doesn't learn, learning off, or the strokes didn't fit the text

entry.name: not_allowed
entry.summary: the person doesn't let this app learn (or hasn't been asked)

entry.name: stale
entry.summary: serial is not the newest candidates of this object

entry.name: unavailable
entry.summary: the service isn't there

entry.name: region_name
entry.summary: a live region of this object already has that name

request.name: get_region

description.summary: a new writing region on the surface

request.description: A handwritten field of its own, named by the app (UTF-8, at most 256 bytes, unique among this object's live regions). It starts in the mode set_mode last gave all regions (ink at first), with an empty rectangle (it takes no stroke until set_rect), no clip, no guides, purpose normal, the person's languages, reading on, neatening off, layer 0. The object enters region mode (above). A region costs the handwriting service nothing until it holds writing.

entry.name: ink
entry.summary: the field takes pen strokes

entry.name: text
entry.summary: the field is a text field the system's keyboard edits; it takes no pen strokes

request.name: set_mode

description.summary: every region of the surface into a mode

request.description: As glassine_handwriting_region_v1.set_mode on each live region, and the mode regions made later start in.

interface.name: glassine_handwriting_region_v1

description.summary: a writing region: one handwritten field on a surface

interface.description:
A field the person fills by hand (GlassineOS/handwriting spec 005). Its strokes, ruled lines and word layout are in the region's own coordinates: x and y from the region's top left corner (set_rect), so the app can move the region (a scroll, a new layout) without anything in it changing, and a move or a resize never causes its writing to be read again.
A stroke belongs, whole, to the region it starts in, wherever it ends, and is read only there. Where regions overlap, the one with the highest layer gets it, and of equal layers the one made last. A region in text mode takes no stroke (also not where it covers another). A stroke still being written when its region is destroyed, or its object or surface goes, is dropped: no event is sent for it.
A region where it takes strokes is also an ink area of its surface (glassine_ink_v1): the panel shows the pen's raw stroke there while it is written, as fast as in any ink area, with the brush of the surface's ink object when the app set one. The app registers nothing for it. A surface whose object is in region mode shows that preview only there and in ink areas the app set itself.
Strokes are numbered per region and never reused: live strokes from 0 up, each one above the highest number the region has used or been handed back (restore). Points are as in the protocol's description, in region coordinates, and come in points parts as there.
Every stroke is sent raw at pen-up (stroke), by the compositor itself, also with reading off (a drawing area) and in a private field. With neatening on, neat_stroke follows as on glassine_handwriting_v1. With reading on, the region has a value: its text, sent whole whenever it changes, with which strokes make which word, the words set in the person's font, the strokes that left the field and the saved state, all ended by one value event. At a pause candidates follow.
Private fields (purpose password or pin, the hints hidden_text or sensitive_data): nothing about the region reaches the handwriting service, no value, candidate, gesture or neat stroke comes, reports answer not_kept; a region that becomes private is forgotten by the service at once. Its raw strokes still come.
Data parts: data_part events gather, per kind, until the event that takes that kind ends them (word, gone and gesture take strokes, set_word shape, value text and state, candidate text); kinds a message doesn't take stay gathered for the next one that does. add_data requests gather in the same way until the request that takes them (edit and report text, restore text and state).

request.name: destroy

description.summary: the field is gone

request.description: The handwriting service forgets its writing at once, no event is sent for it afterwards, and a stroke being written in it is dropped.

request.name: set_rect

description.summary: where the region lies on the surface

request.description: The region's top left corner on the surface and its size (wl_fixed, surface coordinates). The region takes strokes that start inside this rectangle and inside the clip. A move changes nothing else; a new size changes the region's writing area for strokes that follow, and what it holds stays.

request.name: set_clip

description.summary: where on the surface the region takes strokes

request.description: A wl_region in surface coordinates, copied: the part of the region that is visible (the rest scrolled out of view or covered). Null (the start): the whole rectangle. Stated in surface coordinates, a viewport's clip stays the same while its content scrolls.

request.name: set_guides

description.summary: the field's ruled lines, in region coordinates

request.description: As glassine_handwriting_v1.set_guides, with first in region coordinates. A ruled line is a size reference only for this region; a region never takes a line from another. spacing 0: none.

request.name: set_context

description.summary: the field's type and languages

request.description: purpose and hints as in zwp_text_input_v3; languages a comma-separated list in order (empty: the person's setting). Applies to writing that follows.

request.name: set_reading

description.summary: reading on or off

request.description: Off: no value, candidates or gestures for writing that follows; the region still gets its raw strokes (a drawing area), and neat strokes with neatening on.

request.name: set_neaten

description.summary: neatening on or off, and its strength

request.description: As glassine_handwriting_v1.set_neaten; it also applies to the writing the region holds.

description.summary: the stacking order: higher is on top (0 at the start)

request.name: set_mode

description.summary: ink mode or text mode

request.description: In text mode the region takes no pen strokes; the app shows its value as an ordinary text field edited through the system's text input (zwp_text_input_v3) for the region's field type and languages. Before going back to ink mode the app sends the edited text with edit.

entry.name: text
entry.summary: UTF-8 text

entry.name: state
entry.summary: the saved state: opaque bytes the app keeps and hands back unchanged

entry.name: strokes
entry.summary: stroke numbers, uint32 each (events only)

entry.name: shape
entry.summary: a path in region coordinates (path_op), int32 each (events only)

request.name: add_data

description.summary: a part of a text or a saved state for the next request taking it

request.description: At most 2048 bytes a part; the parts of one kind add up until edit, report or restore takes them. Text: at most 65536 bytes in all; state: at most 1 MiB.

request.name: edit

description.summary: the person's text for the field, set by keyboard

request.description: The text gathered in data parts (empty: none) becomes the region's value: a correction of the words whose ink it changed. Unchanged words keep their ink, edited and added ones are set in the person's font; a value event follows with the word layout.

request.name: report

description.summary: what the person did with the field's writing

request.description: serial names a value (accepted: the value as it is; corrected: the text gathered in data parts) or the candidates of one (picked: rank, 0 the best). It applies to the writing that value was read from, never to writing added later, and the ink stays the field's content. discarded is answered not_kept. The answer is report_done.

request.name: restore_points

description.summary: a part of a stored stroke's points

request.description: At most 128 points, in region coordinates, as in the protocol's description; the parts add up until restore_stroke.

request.name: restore_stroke

description.summary: a stored stroke, with its number

request.description: The points gathered since the last restore_stroke are the stored stroke numbered stroke (the number it had when the app kept it). It waits for restore.

request.name: restore

description.summary: hand back stored ink

request.description: The region's writing is replaced by the stored strokes given since the last restore (none: the region is emptied), with the value (text data parts) and the saved state (state data parts) the app kept with them, or neither (strokes alone). The strokes are read with the model the system has now; words the saved state names as confirmed or edited stay as they are. A value event follows. No stroke event is sent for stored strokes; neat_stroke is, with neatening on. A stroke number given twice keeps the last.

description.summary: a part of a stroke's points

event.name: stroke

description.summary: a raw stroke, sent when the pen lifts

event.description: Every stroke that starts in the region, as the tablet reported it, in region coordinates: the points events just before it.

description.summary: the neatened version of a stroke

event.name: data_part

description.summary: a part of a payload for the next event taking it

event.description: At most 2048 bytes a part, gathered per kind as in the interface's description.

event.name: word

description.summary: a word of the value shown as the person's ink

event.description: Part of the value serial: the bytes start to start + length of its text are this word, made of the strokes gathered in strokes data. The app draws them moved by dx, dy (wl_fixed, region coordinates; 0 unless an edited word before it on its line changed width), raw or neat as the region's neatening has it.

entry.name: move
entry.summary: x y

entry.name: line
entry.summary: x y

entry.name: quad
entry.summary: control x y, end x y

entry.name: cubic
entry.summary: two controls, end: six coordinates

entry.name: close
entry.summary: no coordinates

event.name: set_word

description.summary: a word of the value set in the person's font

event.description: Part of the value serial: the bytes start to start + length of its text are this word, which has no ink (typed, or edited by keyboard). Its outline is the shape gathered in shape data: path_op codes, each followed by its coordinates (wl_fixed, region coordinates), filled with the non-zero rule. x, y, width, height: its box, in region coordinates. The app draws it; it never needs the font itself.

event.name: gone

description.summary: strokes that left the field for good

event.description: Part of the value serial: the strokes gathered in strokes data were struck out, replaced by an edit or made a gesture. They are no longer the region's; the app stops drawing and keeping them.

event.name: value

description.summary: the field's value, whole, with its layout

event.description: Ends the value serial (it grows with each value of the region): its text is the text gathered in data parts (lines separated by a newline, in reading order), its saved state the state gathered. The word, set_word and gone events of serial just before it, in the text's order, are its layout; together they are one update, drawn in one go.

event.name: candidate

description.summary: one ranked alternative for the value serial, at a pause

event.description: Its text the text gathered in data parts. rank 0 is the best; origin and fit as on glassine_handwriting_v1.candidate. A pick (report picked) becomes the value.

description.summary: the candidates above (count of them) are complete

entry.name: strike
entry.summary: a strike-through: deletes the words it covers

entry.name: scratch
entry.summary: a scratch-out: deletes the words it covers

entry.name: caret
entry.summary: marks where the next writing is inserted

event.name: gesture

description.summary: a gesture the person wrote in the field

event.description: Made of the strokes gathered in strokes data; it acts only in this region and its strokes are never part of the value. Its effect comes with the value serial.
